data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002's flock-synchrony analogy transfers phase-locking through a shared external signal, but its own overturn condition admits that phase-locking may require direct communication and not emerge from shared external signals alone. The argument never supplies the evidence that would decide whether decentralized-service correlation is actually phase-locked coupling (the transferred mechanism) versus mere common-cause correlation under a shared environment. Because the problem asks for evidence distinguishing truly independent failures from merely-appearing-uncorrelated ones, an argument whose central mechanism rests on an empirically undecided transfer (and concedes the transfer can fail) cannot establish the claimed strict resilience; it also cannot tell us what observation would falsify apparent independence versus hidden coupling beyond listing counterconditions it doesn't test.
